description: Hola, estamos desarrollando una plataforma interactiva que transforma datos científicos de la NASA (como la temperatura oceánica, niveles de CO2 o imágenes satelitales) en experiencias sonoras y visuales. El objetivo es traducir datos complejos en paisajes sonoros accesibles, permitiendo al usuario "escuchar" los cambios de la Tierra.
summary: We developed a web platform that transforms complex datasets from NASA’s Earth Information Center into an intuitive, cognitively and sensorially accessible audiovisual experience, that replaces traditional visual graphs and robotic sounds with realistic and natural environmental soundscapes, generated sea surface temperature and precipitation data. Designed under universal accessibility principles, our platform empowers over 31 615 million visually impaired Peruvians as well as more than 67,000 artisanal fishermen, coastal agricultural communities and coastal workers with limited digital literacy who struggle to interpret complex scientific charts. Using the "El Niño" phenomenon as a critical case study, we deliver faster and easier-to-understand warnings than local organizations or mass media, while protecting marine ecosystems and promoting sustainable fishing. Turning satellite data into accessible sea soundscapes means bridging the information gap, promoting ocean conservation and ensuring a resilient future for our coastal communities.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

  • The interface combines easy-to-read information about what is happening in the ocean powered by OPEN DATA NASA and a brief audio description.

What benefits does it have?

Social: It empowers visually impaired people and fishermen to understand OPEN DATA NASA, also it can function as a interactive plataform from many people.

Eviromental: It is a web plataform that promotes protecting marine ecosystems and sustainable fishing.

Economic: With predictions about the weather, it provides alerts who preventing high-cost for fishermen and seaworks.

What is the intended impact of the project?

To provide visually impaired and fishermen people a way to understand the data in a more dynamic approach.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Tools: Kokoro TTS, Magenta RT2, .
  • Coding languages: Javascript, Python, Three.js library, Apple Mac for MLX machine learning.
  • Hardware: Laptops.
  • Software: Opencode with Claude Sonnet via API.

How is your project creative?

  • It is a interface with ocean heat map with bright red, orange, and yellow to show the sea temperature.
  • It includes natural sounds that help give a idea what is happening
  • It has text to speech description of the current state of the Earth according to the OPEN NASA DATA.

What factors did your team consider?

Include people with audio and visually impairments considering protection of marine biodiversity and coastal agricultural communities.
